flags.title: HIP 2.0 POWER Account — Monthly Contribution Required or Lockout Risk
flags.summary: Indiana's Medicaid expansion, HIP 2.0, requires monthly POWER Account contributions. Failure to pay for 60 days results in a 6-month lockout from HIP Plus, the full benefits tier. Enrollees are dropped to HIP Basic, which has no vision or dental and requires copays. At intake, it is crucial to assess the client's HIP status, contribution currency, and any imminent lockout risk. Contributions are waived for incomes below 100% FPL.

flags.title: Indiana SNAP ABAWD Work Requirements — Active Statewide
flags.summary: Statewide, Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) aged 18–54 must document 80 hours/month of qualifying work activity to receive SNAP benefits. It is important to immediately surface any exemptions, such as disability, caregiving, pregnancy, or enrollment in education or job training. For rural clients, the SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) program is the primary pathway to a waiver.

flags.title: Indiana Minimum Wage — $7.25/hr Federal Floor Only
flags.summary: Indiana's minimum wage is the federal minimum of $7.25/hr, with no state or local increases. This is the lowest in the region. Wage theft is a significant issue, and back wages should be calculated against the federal minimum and FLSA overtime rules. It is recommended to file wage theft claims with both the Indiana Department of Labor and the federal Wage and Hour Division (WHD).

flags.title: Indiana TANF (TANF Cash Assistance) — $288/mo Max, 24-Month Limit
flags.summary: Indiana's TANF program provides a maximum of $288/month for a family of three and has a 24-month lifetime limit, which is shorter than the federal 60-month limit. It is critical to verify the remaining months for any client with a prior Indiana TANF history. The program also has a 20-hour/week work requirement.

flags.title: Indiana Eviction Process — 10-Day Notice, Fast Timeline
flags.summary: Indiana law allows for a 10-day notice for nonpayment of rent, with a total eviction timeline of approximately 3–4 weeks. There is no statewide just-cause eviction requirement. It is recommended to contact legal aid within 5 days of receiving any eviction notice.

flags.title: Indiana Civil Rights — ICRC 180-Day SOL
flags.summary: The Indiana Civil Rights Commission (ICRC) has a 180-day statute of limitations for filing complaints, which is shorter than the EEOC's 300-day deadline. It is recommended to file with the EEOC simultaneously to preserve federal rights. The Indiana Human Rights Law does not include sexual orientation or gender identity as protected classes, so LGBTQ+ workplace discrimination claims should be filed only with the EEOC.

flags.title: Indiana UI — $390/Week Maximum, Lowest in Region
flags.summary: Indiana's maximum unemployment insurance (UI) benefit is $390/week, and the appeal deadline is a very tight 10 days from the determination mailing date. It is recommended to contact legal aid within 5 days of any denial.

flags.title: Lake County / Gary — Chicago Proximity Creates Cross-State Resource Complexity
flags.summary: Lake County, Indiana, is part of the Chicago metro area, which can create complex legal and resource situations for residents who work or have employers in Illinois. It is important to check for the applicability of Illinois and Chicago laws and to connect with resources in both states.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Indiana Emergency Detention
flags.message: IN involuntary psychiatric hold law: Indiana Emergency Detention. Statutory authority: IC 12-26-4. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others or gravely disabled. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in IN retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in IN: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Indiana Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Indiana Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
